scope: Clarify rational analytic types versus real-parameter local logarithmic presentations in Chapters16 and19, preserving the divisorial and local Bergman estimates.
formal_statement_change: lem:bergman-divisorial-error: replace analytic-type terminology in the consequence with its explicit logarithmic presentation; keep the real-parameter inequality unchanged.

edits.old: Consequently, an analytic weight of type $(1/m,\mathcal I(mu))$ has divisorial Lelong number tending to $\nu_E(u)$ as $m\to\infty$.
edits.new: Consequently, a local logarithmic presentation $a_m=m^{-1}\log\sum_k|f_{m,k}|^2+O(1)$, where the $f_{m,k}$ generate $\mathcal I(mu)$, satisfies $\nu_E(a_m)\to\nu_E(u)$ as $m\to\infty$.

edits.old: This implies $k+A_U(E)>m\nu_E(u)$. In particular the weaker non-strict lower bound in the statement holds. Take the minimum over a finite set of local generators and use nonnegativity of the order. The last assertion now follows by letting $m\to\infty$.
edits.new: This implies $k+A_U(E)>m\nu_E(u)$. In particular the weaker non-strict lower bound in the statement holds. Take the minimum over a finite set of local generators and use nonnegativity of the order. Since $\nu_E(a_m)=m^{-1}\operatorname{ord}_E\mathcal I(mu)$, the last assertion follows by letting $m\to\infty$.
For rational $m>0$, the presentation $a_m$ has analytic singularities in the convention of the source book. The real-parameter estimate does not require this restriction.

edits.old: The same local construction and estimates hold for every real parameter $m>0$; only the global sequence below is indexed by integers.
edits.new: The same local construction and estimates hold for every real parameter $m>0$. Its local logarithmic presentation has coefficient $1/m$; this coefficient is rational exactly when $m$ is rational. We use the term analytic type only with the rational-coefficient convention above. The global sequence below is indexed by integers.
